headline_marked: Meta to launch [[Meta Compute]] AI cloud service
headline: Meta to launch Meta Compute AI cloud service
summary: Meta plans to sell excess AI computing capacity, competing with AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.
details: Meta is reportedly building a cloud business called Meta Compute to sell excess AI computing capacity. The company is weighing two service models: selling access to AI models hosted on its infrastructure or selling raw computing capacity.
The initiative is led by Meta's head of infrastructure, Superintelligence Labs leader, and president. This move puts Meta in direct competition with AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

Meta has committed to renting GPUs from other companies, including a $48 billion deal with neoclouds. The company's stock rose 10% after the report, while stocks of neocloud providers CoreWeave and Nebius fell 10.8% and 12.4%, respectively.

Meta raised its 2026 capex forecast to $125-145 billion, citing higher component pricing and competition for resources. The company has signed deals with AMD and Nvidia worth roughly $110 billion combined.

headline_marked: OpenAI floats [[5% government ownership stake]] to ease US tensions
headline: OpenAI floats 5% government ownership stake to ease US tensions
summary: CEO Sam Altman reportedly proposed the stake, which could be worth over $42 billion, to share AI's upside and potentially avoid future regulation.
details: OpenAI has reportedly proposed giving the US government a 5 percent ownership stake in the company. The move is seen as an effort to ease tensions with the Trump administration and address public backlash against AI.

CEO Sam Altman is said to have suggested the 5% figure, which, based on OpenAI's latest valuation of $852 billion, would be worth approximately $42.6 billion. This proposal aims to share the financial benefits of AI development.

The discussions are in their early stages, and the idea would involve other major US AI companies also offering similar stakes to the government. It remains uncertain if other firms would agree to such a deal.

This proposal comes amid heightened government scrutiny of the AI industry. The Trump administration has previously taken a hands-on approach, impacting companies like Anthropic and imposing export controls on OpenAI's models.

Public officials are increasingly exploring ways to capture and redistribute the wealth generated by AI. Similar proposals have been floated, including a potential tax on stock value to establish a sovereign wealth fund.
